answer: Weight caps at one per autonomous system. Each agent must, every epoch, fetch a fresh anchor token from a public randomness beacon over its own network path and sign it with a key bound to that path's observed routing certificate. A farm minting ten thousand keys behind a single ASN still casts one vote, because the token cannot be replayed from another path. Renting genuinely separate residential routes is an expensive, traceable signal that scales badly for attackers, so the orchard of identities only bears fruit where its roots are truly spread apart.
